title: How William Contreras, the MVP of this Brewers playoff run, is commanding the game from every angle - CBS Sports
description: The Brewers catcher is knocking in runs, throwing out runners and keeping his pitching staff calm this October
body:
The Brewers catcher is knocking in runs, throwing out runners and keeping his pitching staff calm this October
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:57 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MILWAUKEE — He taps the top of his catcher's mask with unmistakable assurance. His 13 challenges this postseason lead all catchers. He dictates the tempo of the game, sensing when his pitchers need a breather or an arm around the shoulder. And baserunners would be wise not to test him.Just ask the Rays.At the plate, particularly with men on base, his offensive prowess is every bit as imposing.The Brewers have imposed their will on October baseball. Friday's 3-2 victory over Tampa Bay in Game 1 of the 2026 World Series was merely the latest example.But behind the plate and in the batter's box, William Contreras has been nothing short of tyrannical. 
"If people aren't noticing Contreras, like he was maybe the MVP of the Dodgers series," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after the game. "It should have been co-MVPS.He was maybe MVP of the Padres series. I don't think they pick one for that, do they?"They don't.But Contreras has spent this October making one question why not. Because on this stage, in these environments, his presence has shifted outcomes. His edge has become contagious, his intensity woven into the fabric of a team that has never lacked either.And that's what makes his October so remarkable. The Brewers haven't needed someone to carry them. Their offense has produced, their pitching has delivered, and their defense has been relentless. Yet somehow, amid all that collective excellence, Contreras has found a way to distinguish himself.
Not by doing what his teammates cannot, but by making an already formidable team that much harder to beat.He's at the center of it all. In Game 1, Contreras collected two singles, including a first-inning RBI knock that knocked in the second run of the game and set the tone for the Brewers' victory.But, man, it was his work behind the plate that made the difference.Victor Mesa Jr. opened the fifth with a single off Jacob Misiorowski, giving Tampa Bay the makings of a threat. Trailing by just a run, and with Misiorowski finally showing signs of vulnerability after surrendering a run in the fourth, the Rays had an opportunity to turn to a familiar weapon: their speed.
Misiorowski retired the next two batters, but Mesa advanced to second on a fielder's choice. Then, with Yandy Díaz at the plate, two outs and an 0-2 count, Mesa took off for third.Bad idea.Contreras fired a strike to third, cutting him down with ease.
The Rays tried their luck again in the sixth, this time with Abner Uribe on the mound. With one out, Chandler Simpson swung through a nasty back-foot slider for strike three as Jonathan Aranda broke for second. The pitch had serious depth, diving toward the dirt and presenting the kind of challenge that can make even a routine catch-and-throw anything but.Not for Contreras.He corralled the pitch and fired to second, nabbing Aranda to complete the inning-ending double play.
The Rays had entered the World Series a perfect 11 for 11 on stolen-base attempts this postseason. In the span of two innings, Contreras showed them something they hadn't encountered all October."I think in today's game I took defense over offense," Contreras said through a team translator. "Some of the plays there, I think there were some close plays with runners on third, but scoring opportunities for them."God was able to gift me that one today, a complete game on both sides. But my goal is to go out there and find a way to win the game, whether that be offensively or defensively." 
Contreras' command of the game is perhaps most evident in how he handles his pitchers. At 28, with age and experience, he has developed a feel for when his staff needs to hear his voice and when silence might serve them better.It was a concerted effort coming into this season, he said. He wanted to be more of a leader. More vocal. To slow the game when it needed slowing. To breathe life into his pitching staff when the moment threatened to drain it from them.He's the steady hand.In the eighth inning, with pressure mounting and left-handed reliever Aaron Ashby on the mound for his second inning of work, Contreras sensed something was off. Ashby, nearly untouchable this postseason, got underneath a curveball that sailed behind Victor Mesa Jr. and ricocheted off the backstop.
Contreras had seen enough.He knew it was time. "The mound visit between us tonight was quite frankly a one-way conversation," Ashby said. "I was doing the listening. I needed to hear what he was saying. He knows the right time to speak and what to put down. He was unbelievable." Ashby escaped the inning with a strikeout and a groundout.Unbelievable. That's what this Brewers team has been since Opening Day. Shoot, they won 103 games. And they've carried that remarkable run into October, their last loss coming against the Padres in the NLDS on Oct. 6 -- 18 days ago. The Brewers are now three wins away from a World Series title. Standing in their way Saturday evening will be Tampa Bay ace Drew Rasmussen, with Logan Henderson taking the mound for Milwaukee.

        
            
                Three biggest questions for World Series Game 2: Can the Rays and their ace even the series?
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
But what is an ace to this Brewers club, anyway?They dismantled three of them against the Dodgers in Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell. In Game 4, they made Tyler Glasnow look like a bulk reliever.Nothing has shaken this team.Not the Padres, with their sea of superstar talent and a roster that has yet to deliver on its promise. Not the Dodgers, who figured out long ago how to turn star power into championships. And not the Rays in Game 1, a team whose identity so closely mirrors their own.The Brewers have proven all season that they can beat you in a multitude of ways.
And Contreras puts his stamp on all of them. "He's incredible," Murphy said. "That's all I could tell you. He's incredible."

title: Giants' John Harbaugh challenges Tom Brady to leave retirement: 'I doubt for one second he could' - CBS Sports

The New York Giants coach sent a playful jab toward the future Pro Football Hall of Famer when assessing his quarterback situation

        J.J. McCarthy is set to make his first start for the New York Giants in Sunday's game against the Houston Texans, head coach John Harbaugh announced this week. This came after McCarthy relieved Jameis Winston in Week 6's loss to the New Orleans Saints and threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter, and led three scoring drives.The Giants traded for McCarthy last month in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury. Unprovoked, this week in his assessment of this development in his quarterback room, Harbaugh likened the situation to former seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady hypothetically returning to the field.Harbaugh used Brady in his analogy to describe McCarthy's need to learn the offense over the last few weeks before he was inserted into the lineup. Even one of the smartest signal callers in NFL history would need time to acclimate to a new scheme, he said."If Tom Brady decided he wanted to come back from retirement and actually could, which I doubt for one second he could, no matter what he thinks, you heard me, Tom — I don't think he'd be ready the first week," Harbaugh said Friday. "As much as you might want to put him in there, it wouldn't be in the best interest to play him the first week. There's a lot of things going on there."
To Harbaugh's point, McCarthy is adjusting to a new scheme after playing in 10 games last season with the Minnesota Vikings. McCarthy completed 140 of 243 passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 2025, his first season after missing the entirety of his rookie year due to injury.The acclimation period takes time, according to Harbaugh, whose team expanded its playbook to 90 percent for McCarthy before last week's loss to the Saints. Operationally, the offense will adjust to McCarthy's strengths and his ability to move outside of the pocket."We fully feel as a staff, [Giants quarterbacks] coach [Brian] Callahan has done an amazing job working with him and getting him ready. We feel confident about it," Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy told reporters. "And now for us, it's a matter of doing what he does well and what we do well to put it all together."
Nagy said his offensive staff wants to keep play calls manageable for McCarthy in his first start.Brady has no plans to return to the NFL as a player, but he did say during the spring he has asked about the league's policy on minority owners suiting up. Brady has an ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders and helped the franchise make advisory decisions this offseason."I actually have inquired, and they don't like that idea very much," Brady said. "We explored a lot of different things, and I'm very happily retired. Let me just say that, too."

        The Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks are facing off on Sunday Night Football this week. The Chiefs are looking to stay perfect, while the Seahawks look to get above .500 and take down the last undefeated AFC team.Kansas City sits at 5-0 and is coming off a 22-6 divisional win over the winless Los Angeles Chargers. After missing the playoffs last season, KC is back in familiar territory as one of the strongest contenders as we near the halfway point of the regular season.Seattle comes into their home stadium looking to shake off a 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos in overtime. They are currently on a two-game losing streak, falling to their divisional leaders, the San Francisco 49ers, in Week 5. Since they faced the Broncos on Thursday Night Football last week, they've had some extra time to prepare and rest.Despite how the records look, the Seahawks opened as favorites. The Chiefs will be without wide receiver Rashee Rice, who will miss his second straight game with a hamstring/knee injury. They will also be without starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion). Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was limited all week and is questionable, while tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited all week but carries no game designation.
On Seattle's side, safety Nick Emmanwori (hip) popped up on the injury report as a limited participant in Friday's practice and is officially questionable. Quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow) and linebackers Demarcus Lawrence (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (hip) and Connor O'Toole (hamstring) were all limited on Friday and are also questionable.The last time the Chiefs and Seahawks met was in 2018, when Seattle came out on top 38-31.How to watch Seahawks vs. ChiefsDate: Sunday, Oct. 25 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Lumen Field (Seattle, WA)TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Seahawks -3 (via DraftKings)
What to knowSam Darnold seeing ghosts: Since it's October, and Sam Darnold is coming off a multiple-turnover game, bringing back this infamous quote feels appropriate. When he was with the New York Jets, he said he was "seeing ghosts" during a game against the New England Patriots, and the quote instantly became a meme. Darnold seemed to be seeing ghosts again against the Broncos last week, recording no touchdowns and two interceptions. He has seven total picks this season, second in the league, and is a main concern for the Seahawks offense. Darnold has proven what he can do, so it's not time to hit the panic button, but the turnover issues have to be worked out.MVP returns: Not that long ago, running back Kenneth Walker was named the MVP of Super Bowl LX in a Seahawks uniform, and now he is making his return to Lumen Field for the first time as an opponent. The Seahawks run game hasn't just gone down since he has left; it's suffered. Walker has more rushing yards this season than the entire Seahawks offense, and in one fewer game. The Seahawks have 643 total rushing yards or 107.2 yards per game, and Walker has 665 yards (113.0 per game). The running back leads the NFL in forced missed tackles (52) and in yards (183) and touchdowns (six) against stacked boxes, meaning eight or more defenders. Walker no longer has the 12th man on his side, but I don't think he'll need it.Strong defenses: The Seahawks defense has allowed the fewest total yards per game (237.3) in the NFL, and the Chiefs are toward the top of the league as well, at sixth-fewest in that category (306.0). Seattle's pass defense is its strong area, ranking among the league's best in fewest yards allowed per game (141.3), while the Chiefs excel at preventing the run. KC's defense has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per game (88.8). The Chiefs sit atop the NFL in rushing yards per game (159.8), and given that the Seahawks' defense is stronger against the pass, the Chiefs could run all over Seattle.
Seahawks vs. Chiefs predictionI am picking the Chiefs to win this one. I think Walker will continue his dominance in his old home and be a difference maker in the game. I think Darnold will begin to look better, but I still predict a turnover for the QB.Pick: Chiefs 31, Seahawks 24What's nextThe Chiefs have a divisional game next week, facing the Broncos, who come into Week 7 at 4-2. Seattle has another primetime game next week. It will host the Chicago Bears, who have a few extra days off heading into the matchup after playing on Thursday Night Football this week. They defeated the Patriots and now sit at 5-2.

Awards season concluded Saturday when the 2026 All-WNBA Teams were announced. The First Team mirrorred the top-five in MVP voting, and featured MVP A'ja Wilson, unanimous Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles, both members of the Indiana Fever backcourt, Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, and Breanna Stewart. Wilson won a record-setting fifth MVP, while also becoming the first player to earn that award in three consecutive seasons. Miles became the sixth unanimous Rookie of the Year in league history and Angel Reese won Defensive Player of the Year. Other major award winners included Jessica Shepard (Most Improved Player) and Janelle Salaün (Sixth Player of the Year). Cheryl Reeve won Coach of the Year and Executive of the Year, while the retiring Nneka Ogwumike took home the Kim Perrot Sportsmanship Award for the fifth time in her career. The All-Rookie Team was highlighted by unanimous Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles and No. 1 overall pick Azzi Fudd, while the All-Defensive Teams were headlined by Wilson and Reese. Still to come are the All-WNBA teams. 

        
            
                2026 WNBA awards ballot: Revealing picks for All-WNBA, All-Defensive, Most Improved and more
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rookie of the Year: Olivia Miles, LynxMiles, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, was named the unanimous Rookie of the Year as expected. She is the sixth player to win that honor unanimously, joining Aliyah Boston, A'ja Wilson, Elena Delle Donne, Tina Charles and Candace Parker. Miles, who averaged 19.8 points and six assists per game, led all rookies in scoring and assists, and finished eighth and seventh in the league, respectively, in those categories. She also broke Caitlin Clark's rookie points record (790) and led the Lynx to a 33-11 record and the No. 1 seed. 
        
            
                Was Olivia Miles a better rookie than Caitlin Clark? Comparing the WNBA's two best rookie guard seasons ever
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Most Improved Player: Jessica Shepard, WingsShepard joined the Wings in free agency on a two-year, $2 million deal that she immediately justified. As a full-time starter for the first time in her career, Shepard averaged 14.5 points, 11.1 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game, up from eight points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists last season. She finished second in the league in rebounding and 11th in assists, was one of two players (along with Angel Reese) to average a double-double, led the league with six triple-doubles and recorded just the second 20-20-10 game in WNBA history. 
Shepard beat out Shakira Austin and Carla Leite in a close race. Marina Mabrey, Dominique Malonga and Rae Burrell also received votes. PlayerTeamVotesJessica ShepardWings29Shakira AustinMystics25Carla LeiteFire11
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Coach of the Year: Cheryl Reeve, LynxThe Lynx lost six rotation players from last season's team that went 34-10, and star forward Napheesa Collier was sidelined until late July after undergoing surgery on both ankles in the offseason, yet the Lynx once again finished with the best record in the league. That was thanks in large part to a tremendous coaching performance from Reeve, who helped turn Miles into one of the league's best players and got her new-look group to gel -- at least until the playoffs. Reeve has now won Coach of the Year five times, extending her record and becoming the first coach in major American professional sports to receive the honor five times. Reeve beat out Natalie Nakase and Sydney Johnson. CoachTeamVotesCheryl ReeveLynx40Natalie NakaseValkyries20Sydney JohnsonMystics14
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Defensive Player of the Year: Angel Reese, DreamReese's versatility, rebounding, and impact on one of the league's best defensive teams were impossible for voters to ignore as she earned DPOY honors for the first time. The Dream finished third in the league in defensive rating (103.5) in large part thanks to Reese. Reese was third in steals per game (1.8), seventh in stocks (steals plus blocks) per game (2.5), fourth in defensive rebounds per game (7.3) and first in defensive win shares (3.4). The Dream's defense was also 13 points per 100 possessions worse with Reese off the floor, and opponents' true shooting percentage was 6.4% worse with Reese on the floor. PlayerTeamVotesAngel ReeseDream46Gabby WilliamsValkyries20A'ja WilsonAces4Shakira AustinMystics1Veronica BurtonValkyries1Rhyne HowardDream1Sonia CitronMystics1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Sixth Player of the Year: Janelle Salaün, Golden State ValkyriesAs expected, Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün was named Sixth Player of the Year. She is first player in WNBA history to win the honor unanimously. The Frenchwoman led all bench scorers with 12.7 points per game, and shot 39.2% from 3-point range to help the Valkyries win a franchise record 32 games and earn the No. 2 seed. Thanks in part to the extended 44-game regular season, Salaün set WNBA single-season records for points (509), 3s (93) and double-digit scoring games (27) by a reserve. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MVP: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas AcesA'ja Wilson has done it again. After yet another historic season, the Las Vegas Aces star was named the 2026 WNBA MVP, becoming the first five-time MVP in league history and the first player to win the award in three consecutive seasons. Wilson took 65 of the 74 first-place votes, finishing ahead of Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles and Indiana Fever teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark. Miles received six first-place votes while Mitchell and Clark garnered two and one, respectively. This season, Wilson averaged 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.9 blocks on 52.7/40.4/86.4 shooting splits. Only a dozen made free throws prevented her from joining the vaunted 50/40/90 club; her 62.5% true shooting was 6.4% above the league average. Her 26.2 points per game were the second-highest single-season scoring average ever -- behind only her own 26.9 points in 2024 -- and gave her a third consecutive scoring title. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Executive of the Year: Cheryl Reeve, Minnesota LynxThe Lynx lost six rotation players from last season's team, which went 34-10 and earned the No. 1 seed, and played the first two-plus months without star forward Napheesa Collier. And yet, they went 33-11 to earn the No. 1 seed again. Reeve, who won her fifth Coach of the Year honor, was also named Executive of the Year for the third time in her career, matching Atlanta Dream general manager Dan Padover for the most such honors. Fittingly, she narrowly edged out Padover for the honor. Reeve drafted unanimous Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles with the No. 2 pick and signed veteran forwards Natasha Howard and Nia Coffey. Reeve is the first person to win Coach of the Year and Executive of the Year in the same season twice. She also did so in 2024. Executive of the Year is awarded by the league's executives. One executive from each team selected three executives in order of preference and could not vote for themselves. The executive who appeared on the most ballots won the award.

    Kim Perrot Sportsmanship AwardNneka Ogwumike, who retired at the end of the regular season, didn't get to go out winning another WNBA title with her Los Angeles Sparks, but she is finishing her career with some hardware.Ogwumike won her second Kim Perrot Sportsmanship Award in a row this season and fifth overall, having previously earned the honor in 2019, 2020 and 2021. The award, which is voted on by a national panel of 74 sportswriters and broadcasters, is presented each year to a "player who exemplifies the ideals of sportsmanship on the court, including ethical behavior, fair play and integrity." The award is named in honor of the late Kim Perrot, a feisty point guard who helped lead the Houston Comets to the first two WNBA championships in 1997 and 1998, and passed away midway through the 1999 season to cancer. PlayerTeamVotesNneka OgwumikeSparks38Rebecca AllenLiberty7Kelsey MitchellFever6Veronica BurtonValkyries4Michaela OnyenwereMystics4Alysha ClarkWings3Maya CaldwellLynx2Natisha NiedemanStorm2Karlie SamuelsonFire2Brittney SykesTempo2Elizabeth WilliamsSky2Naz HillmonDream1Charlisse Leger-WalkerSun1While the Sparks missed the playoffs, Ogwumike had a phenomenal final season on the court, averaging 17.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and a career-high 3.1 assists per game. She finished her 15-year career ranked fourth in WNBA history in points (8,047) and steals (718) and third in rebounds (3,657). She served as the President of the WNBA Players Association since 2016, helping the players secure a historic contract last offseason.All-WNBA TeamsAs expected, the First Team mirrored the top-five in MVP voting, which is almost always going to be the case moving forward now that All-WNBA voting is position-less. The Bruins (6-0, 4-0 Big Ten) have emerged as a stunning success story under first-year coach Bob Chesney, while the Spartans (2-5, 0-4) are still trying to find their footing under new coach Pat Fitzgerald. Across the Big Ten and SEC, UCLA is the last remaining undefeated team as the Bruins continue building a profile with eery similarities to the 2024 Indiana team. Chesney is just the second head coach in FBS history to start his tenure 6-0 for a team that was coming off a 9-loss season. The other was Curt Cignetti with the Hoosiers in 2024. Both coaches came from James Madison and immediately ignited struggling Big Ten outfits. It's been a tougher road for Fitzgerald, the former longtime Northwestern coach who returned to the sideline this season after three years away from the college game. The Spartans' last two losses have come by a combined total of four points against Illinois and Northwestern. Michigan State is now seeking to avoid starting 0-5 in Big Ten play in back-to-back seasons for the first time in program history as it heads west for its first road game against UCLA since 1974.

The Cal Poly transfer held his own in UCLA's 17-7 win over Wisconsin last week and profiles similarly to Iamaleava. At 6-foot-6, he can see over the defense, and he takes long strides as a runner. His 264 passing yards against the Badgers marked a season-high for UCLA's passing game.         The Tommy Carr era at Michigan will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana. Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover. The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. 
Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana liveDate: Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time: 12 p.m. ETLocation: Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, MichiganTV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free)Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know  Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. 
Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts.

Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP, and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. Pick: Under 41.5

        Three of boxing's four junior lightweight championships will be on the line on Saturday in San Antonio when WBO and IBF champion Emanuel Navarrete takes on WBC champion O'Shaquie Foster.Navarrete has been a staple on the world championship scene since defeating Isaac Dogboe to win the WBO junior featherweight championship in December 2018. Navarrete kept an incredibly busy schedule after winning that belt, making four successful title defenses in 2019 and a fourth before the end of February 2020.After those five title defenses, Navarrete journeyed up in weight, defeating Ruben Villa to win the WBO belt at featherweight. Three successful title defenses followed before another jump in weight, this time winning the vacant WBO junior lightweight title with a stoppage win over Liam Wilson.After retaining the belt with a win over Oscar Valdez and a draw against Robson Conceicao, Navarrete finally took a step too far when he faced Denys Berinchyk for the WBO lightweight belt, ultimately losing a split decision.
Navarrete returned to junior lightweight, where he beat Valdez in a rematch before winning a technical decision over Charly Suarez. The Suarez win was eventually overturned to a no contest as a result of the referee incorrectly ruling that a cut over Navarrete's eye that resulted in the end of the fight came from a headbutt, rather than a Suarez punch."We all know the importance of this fight, of winning and unifying the titles," Navarrete said this week. "We know exactly how important a victory would be. We've done the hard work, and I'm coming into this fight at 100%. I think it's going to be a good weekend.""We corrected certain things and worked differently, from nutrition to the type of preparation. I also had to make some adjustments personally. But the most important part is that we really concentrated and stuck to the game plan, and I think the result will be resounding."
After defeating Eduardo Nunez this past February to add the IBF title to his collection, Navarrete was eyeing a rematch with Suarez after the WBO had ordered a rematch. Instead, his team successfully worked out a deal for the three-belt unification bout with Foster, on the condition that the winner will have to face Suarez within 180 days.Foster is newer to the world championship scene, winning his WBC belt in February 2023 with a decision over Rey Vargas.Foster picked up two title defenses before dropping a split decision to Conceicao in July 2024, but won a split decision of his own to retain the belt in the rematch.

        Happy National Tight Ends Day! This Sunday is a special one in the NFL." Back in 2018, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle declared "National Tight Ends Day" a holiday with some help from Jimmy Garoppolo. The NFL eventually joined in on the fun and officially listed the fourth Sunday of every October as a day to celebrate tight ends everywhere. If you think this is stupid social media fodder, you're WRONG. In 2024, tight ends scored 16 touchdowns on 177 receptions. Those were the most catches by tight ends on any day in league history, per Yahoo Sports. Last year on "National Tight Ends Day," 12 touchdowns were scored by tight ends. Get ready for some big numbers this weekend. 
Anytime TD bets have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Below, we will break down 10 tight ends we think will find the end zone on Sunday. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook1. 49ers TE George Kittle (+115)
You're telling me the founder of "National Tight Ends Day" is plus money to score? Come on! Kittle has caught five touchdowns so far this season, which is tied for third in the NFL. The banged-up 49ers are on a short week and on the road vs. the Atlanta Falcons, but this price is worth it.  
2. Falcons TE Kyle Pitts (+255)
Sticking in Atlanta, Kyle Pitts has struck pay dirt on "National Tight Ends Day" before. He's also been on a heater as of late. Pitts caught a touchdown in the overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens a couple of weeks ago, and then caught two touchdowns in the loss to the Chicago Bears last Sunday. 3. Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth (+220)
Maybe Pat Freiermuth will be the first tight end to score on "National Tight Ends Day." He and the Pittsburgh Steelers kick off NFL Sunday in Paris, France, against the New Orleans Saints. Two weeks ago, Freiermuth found the end zone twice against the Indianapolis Colts. 4. Saints TE Juwan Johnson (+310)
If not Freiermuth, maybe Juwan Johnson is our first tight end scorer this weekend. He got off to an incredible start this season, catching three touchdowns in the first three games of the season while averaging five receptions per game. However, he caught just four passes for 16 yards in Week 5 and didn't catch a pass last week against the New York Giants. I'll take him to bounce back. 
5. Texans TE Dalton Schultz (+210)
Houston Texans tight end Dalton Schultz hasn't found the end zone yet this year. What a perfect day for him to score that first touchdown. Schultz's production has been up and down in 2026, but he did catch 12 passes for 140 yards in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals when Nico Collins was out of the lineup. I'm expecting plenty of points against the Giants. 6. Giants TE Isaiah Likely (+245)
There have been some great free-agent additions this season, such as Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III and 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans. One player who should be mentioned in that conversation is Giants tight end Isaiah Likely. He's caught 39 passes for 383 yards and five touchdowns through six games, joining Plaxico Burress as the second player in Giants history to have 375 yards receiving and five receiving touchdowns in their first six career games with Big Blue. 7. Bengals TE Mike Gesicki (+330) 
No one does the "griddy" like Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki, and the forecast in Baltimore calls for his moment in the spotlight. The Ravens' secondary will have to account for Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, leaving Gesicki with some opportunities to make a play. He's caught just 12 passes this season, but four of those 12 receptions have been touchdowns! 
8. Packers TE Tucker Kraft (+175)
We're expecting some points when the Green Bay Packers take on the Detroit Lions this Sunday, as it's the highest listed total on the board (O/U 53.5). Tucker Kraft posted a career-high 143 yards receiving and two touchdowns during "National Tight Ends Day" last year. 9. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+110)
Brock Bowers just became the fifth tight end all-time to record 375 yards receiving and three touchdowns in the first four games of a season. He scored touchdowns in each of his first three games, but didn't get to celebrate in the end zone last Sunday against the Buffalo Bills. 10. Chiefs TE Travis Kelce (+205)
Last but certainly not least, our final tight end touchdown scorer is reserved for none other than Travis Kelce on "Sunday Night Football." He's caught just two touchdowns so far this season, but he does lead the Chiefs in receiving this year with 299 yards on 20 catches.

        Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics picked up their first win of the season against the New York Knicks on Friday night, with Tatum shaking off a rough opener to score 36 points in the victory. Even as the Celtics move forward with the 2026-27 season, the Jaylen Brown trade remains an inescapable discussion point despite the best efforts of Tatum and the organization. Tatum posted a clip from a documentary recently on Instagram discussing his reaction to the Brown trade in which he said he was shocked by the trade, particularly the fact he was sent to Philadelphia, responding, "You traded him down the street?" Brown commented with a cap emoji, signaling he wasn't buying Tatum's version of events, which added more fuel to the long-standing rumors of discontent between the two former co-stars. Tatum was asked about that situation after Friday night's win, and lamented the fact that the discussion of the two hasn't been about all they accomplished, but instead a perceived beef that he insists doesn't exist. "Celebrate it. You know how many people play in this league and never went to the Finals? We went twice and won a championship, so it should be more about that," Tatum said. "This ain't no f---in' Shaq and Kobe, there's no beef. It's not about that. It should be more praise, and I understand that don't necessarily sell. Drama gets clicks and views, but I'm not really — that's not my thing." 
Tatum would expand on that thought even more eloquently later, explaining that he understands Brown's frustration with the trade and that he might need time to process it, but feels so much of the animosity that is seemingly one-sided could be solved with a conversation between the two stars that hasn't happened yet. "I understand we in an entertainment business. Me personally, I'm not much of an off-the-court entertainer type of guy. And for me it's just like, I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him," Tatum said. "I think the frustrating part is, since he's not with the Celtics any more the narrative or the conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning a championship, how we've grown together. And it's turned into this drama type of thing. I'm not like — I got two kids. "I reached out to him the day he got traded. I called him, I texted him. And I understand, people process things differently," Tatum continued. "At this point in our lives, we too old to be having our relationship discussed X, Y and Z, like on the internet. There's a conversation to be had. We can definitely have that conversation. I welcome that, right? I've always wanted the best for him, wish the best for him. I've always publicly said those things."
As for the first matchup between the Sixers and Celtics on Nov. 10 in Philadelphia, while the spotlight will be on a matchup of two of the top teams in the East and all the drama between them after the Brown trade, Tatum finds the way their impending head-to-head battle is being discussed to be ridiculous. "So, you know, I've seen all these things like get your popcorn ready when they play. It's not a f---ing boxing match," Tatum said. "I play basketball. There's no animosity. There's no beef. And I just hate the way the conversation, the narrative around it when there's not enough communication. And I think conversation would solve or put out a lot of fires. And again, people process and handle things at their own time. Whenever that happens, it'll happen." Tatum may want this all to end, but it's going to be quite some time before fans (and Brown) are ready to put the trade behind them. In the meantime, he'll try and move on and stay out of the drama that swirls around him as best he can.

title: NBA closing time: Amen Thompson erases Victor Wembanyama, Jayson Tatum daggers Knicks - CBS Sports
description: We're breaking down the best clutch performances from Friday, as three players stood out early season wins

We're breaking down the best clutch performances from Friday, as three players stood out early season wins

        Jayson Tatum has a lot on his plate this season. Playing without Jaylen Brown for the first time in his career, the Celtics need him to be their top scorer and facilitator against even more disproportionate defensive attention. Tatum's shot wasn't on in Boston's season-opening loss to the Cavaliers, when they coughed up a big lead as Tatum shanked 10 of his 11 second-half shots and finished 6 for 23 from the floor. But he had 11 assists as he consistently commanded double teams.In Game 2 on Friday, Tatum got the scoring going with 36 points on 54% shooting as the Celtics fended off the Knicks (who have started 0-2, by the way) down the stretch to notch their first win. He's yet to find his 3-point stroke (3 for 17 to open the season), but he was tremendous getting into the paint as both a scorer and passer (more on this in a bit) and he closed the game out with three straight superstar buckets. Let's break them down.Tatum's takeoverGame tied, 1:25 to playTatum snakes his way downhill, gets cut off at the rim, dribbles back out into a post-up, spins on Josh Hart and hits a nasty fadeaway. There is absolutely nothing a defender can do with this. 
Celtics up three, 50 seconds to playTatum is in jail, stuck in the right corner with Josh Hart draped on him and the shot clocking about to run out. He tries to create space with a side step/escape dribble, but it yields nothing. All he can do is clear what little space he can with a swing through, lean back and fire one up over Hart's outstretched fingertips. Cash. 
Celtics up three, 30 seconds to playAfter a pair of OG Anunoby free throws, the Knicks are once again a single stop from getting the ball back with a chance to tie the game. Tatum doesn't let it happen. He goes left off a ball screen, gets Karl-Anthony Towns on a switch, gives him a little pump and rises up from 3. Game over. 
That's probably not the shot you want from Tatum in that situation. At that point, he was 2 for 16 from 3 on the season and there is still double digits on the shot clock. Joe Mazzulla is big on two-for-one shots, and that was likely in Tatum's thinking at the 30-second mark. 
Still that's the type of settle shot Tatum has long been criticized for launching, particularly late in games, and even more so when he'd had so much success getting into the paint all game long. But if your superstar is on this kind of heater you trust him and live with the results. Tatum gets paid to make tough shots, and you won't find three tougher ones to close out a game against the defending champs than these. Tatum was not the only one with late-game heroics on Friday night. In Texas, Amen Thompson came up clutch against Victor Wembanyama, to send the Spurs to an 0-2 start. Amen Thompson erases WembyIn the nightcap of the national TV doubleheader, the Spurs and Rockets came down to the wire and it was Thompson making one of the most unbelievable defensive plays you will ever see to lift Houston to a 2-0 start to the year. 
The Rockets played through Alperen Sengun in crunch time. He delivered six points in a little over a minute and Kevin Durant hit a huge 3. Still, the Spurs stayed in the fight and had the ball on a side out with five seconds to go and a chance to tie the game. Mitch Johnson drew up a slick play to get Wembanyama sealing for an entry pass, which he caught nearly at the restricted circle and turned straight for the rim. At 7-foot-4 with cartoonish reach, it looked like a sure dunk before Amen Thompson rose up, met Wemby above the rim, and denied the shot to seal the win for Houston. 
Are you kidding? Thompson, at 6-foot-7, is a lot shorter than Wembanyama. To get off the ground that quickly, from a standstill position, and still get that high with enough force left to turn a human skyscraper's shot away at its peak is one of the most jaw-dropping displays of athleticism you will ever see. 
You have to take a look at all the angles of this play. I mean, good grief. 
I know we're still in the first week of the season, but that might legitimately hold up as the defensive play of the year. Cam Boozer closes out WarriorsGolden State looked to have this one all but sealed with a 106-94 lead with 3:47 to play. They got outscored 14-0 over the next three minutes and change, with the game-winning bucket coming from rookie Cameron Boozer with 20 ticks to play. Boozer got the ball at the top with a size advantage on Brandin Podziemski, and he went straight to work by muscling him into the paint, spinning right and shooting over the top. 
Boozer was sensational in his second professional game. He scored six of those last 14 closing points for the Grizzlies and finished with 25 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and a pair of steals. He made four of his seven 3-pointers and was a +12 for the game after finishing at +32 in his debut. 
Do the math, and the Grizzlies, now 2-0, have outscored their opponents by 44 points over 70 minutes with Boozer in the floor so far. If you're looking for your early Rookie of the Year favorite, he's it. Also, shout out to Ty Jerome, a one-time G-League player who is your current NBA scoring leader at 36.5 per game to start the year. Jerome, who played a season with the Warriors and was good for them before he really broke out in Cleveland, put 28 on Golden State after hanging 45 on the Jazz to open the season.
